This page names the artifacts we write and shows how each one leads to the next, so a counter clerk's idea can be traced all the way to the release note that tells her it shipped.

## When

- Read it when you join the team and before you write your first artifact.
- Come back when two people use one word for different things. Settle it here, then fix the other documents.
- Review it each year at the direction review.

## Who

- **Product manager** owns this document and the roadmap.
- Everyone on the team uses these terms in artifacts, meetings and replies to requesters. So do AI agents working with the team.

## The artifact chain

An **artifact** is anything the team generates as part of designing, building and running a service, made to be used and built on by the next step. The artifacts below connect in a hierarchy, so daily work can be traced back to goals.

| Artifact | What it is | Owner | Usual horizon | Format sentence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Idea** | Raw input from anyone, no commitment | Product manager owns the idea log; anyone adds | None | None. Use the submitter's words |
| **Initiative** | The tracked bet that pursuing an opportunity will move a goal. Holds its Solutions | Product manager | Later until active; then shown through its Solutions and Deliverables | We believe [problem space] represents an opportunity to advance [goal] by [approach hypothesis]. |
| **Solution** | One way of reaching the Initiative's outcome, tested, built, kept or dropped. An Initiative may try several | Product manager decides; product owner helps scope | Next (its slice for this quarter shows in Now as a Deliverable) | [Solution] will enable [user group] to [do something], which we expect to move [the Initiative's outcome]. |
| **Deliverable** | A tangible thing handed over, so a commitment can be checked as met or not. On the roadmap, a slice of a Solution scheduled this quarter | Product manager schedules; product owner runs delivery | Now | None. Use concrete delivery language |
| **User story** | The smallest piece of user value, finished in one sprint | Product owner writes; development team estimates | None | As a [user type], I need to [action], so that I can [benefit]. |
| **Release notes** | Internal and external messages that close the loop on a Deliverable | Product owner; product manager for Solution launches | None | None. Lead with the benefit |
| **Goal** | A change in what people do, with baseline and target, held one to two years | Executive steering group with the product manager | One grid row per goal | By [timeframe], [user group] will [behavior change], measured by [metric], creating [community value]. |

**Epics** sit outside the chain. They are optional containers the team uses to group stories within a Solution, in whatever shape helps (see the Glossary). A story always links to its Deliverable; it may also belong to an epic.

The **roadmap** is the one document that pulls these together. It links to the artifacts and doesn't rewrite them.

## The roadmap

| Section | Holds | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Vision and strategy | Vision; diagnosis, guiding approach, 3-5 key actions, tradeoffs | Yearly |
| Goals and goal progress | Up to three goals and the progress table | Goals yearly, progress quarterly |
| Now/Next/Later grid | Initiatives, Solutions, Deliverables | Quarterly |
| Quarterly commitments | Deliverables and ongoing commitments, intended progress per goal | Set quarterly, status each sprint |
| Sprint report | One row per sprint | Each sprint |

## Definitions

Every term, including the words we avoid, is defined in the [Glossary](/system/glossary). This page shows how the artifacts connect; the glossary says what each word means.

## Template

Trace any piece of work. Each row links to the one above.

| Artifact | Name | Links to | Lives in | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Idea | | Requester, date | Idea log | |
| Initiative | | Ideas, goal | Initiative artifact | |
| Solution | | Initiative | Initiative's Solutions list | |
| Deliverable | | Solution | Quarterly commitments | Committed / On track / Off track / Done |
| User story | | Deliverable (and epic, if the team uses one) | Sprint | |
| Release notes | | Deliverable | Sent to | |

## DMV example

| Artifact | DMV entry |
|---|---|
| Idea | "Show a document checklist before someone comes in for a new license." Counter clerk, Jan 15. Triaged as an idea for improvement, tagged to Goal 2. |
| Initiative | Single-trip new driver licenses. We believe repeat trips for standard new driver license applications represent an opportunity to advance Goal 2 (zero multi-trip experiences, baseline 85%) by helping applicants know they are ready before they come in. Framed at Q2 planning and still active. |
| Solution | The second one tried. A document checklist was prototyped first and dropped. License Ready Check will enable first-time applicants to confirm before their visit that their documents will be accepted, which we expect to move the repeat-trip rate. Building from Q3. Size XL (5+ sprints), sliced across three quarters. |
| Deliverable | Pre-check for birth certificates and proof of address: photo upload and staff review for the two most common problem documents. Now, Q3. Committed. |
| User story | As a first-time applicant, I need to submit a photo of my birth certificate before my visit, so that I can find out whether it will be accepted. |
| Release notes | External: "Before your license visit, you can now send us a photo of your birth certificate or proof of address. We'll tell you within two business days if it will be accepted." Internal: counter staff see reviewed documents on the appointment record. |

The clerk who logged the idea in January gets the release note too.

## Rules of thumb

- If you can't name it specifically, you don't understand it well enough to put it on the roadmap.
- One item, one column. "Phase 1" in Now, "phase 2" in Next and "phase 3" in Later is one item pretending to be three.
- Lightweight capture, rigorous connection. Ideas cost nothing to log. Everything after an Idea links to its parent.
- If work won't fit the user story format, you probably haven't found the right artifact yet.
- Link, don't copy. Artifacts point at research and specs. They don't repeat them.
